questions.question: In a classroom activity, students use green and white cocktail sticks on a green lawn to model natural selection. What does picking up more white sticks than green ones demonstrate?
options: How predators easily spot prey that is not camouflaged
How organisms learn to change their colour
How plants compete for light
How fossils are mineralised over millions of years

questions.question: If a green lawn becomes covered in white frost and snow, how would the prediction in the cocktail stick model change?
options: Green sticks will be easier to see and collected more quickly
White sticks will be easier to see and collected more quickly
Neither colour will be visible to the predator
Both colours will become equally camouflaged

questions.question: What is the scientific term for the special features that make a species well suited to survive in its environment?
options: Habitats
Variations
Adaptations
Generations

questions.question: How does having thick, insulating blubber provide an advantage to a seal living in the freezing Arctic?
options: It helps the seal to breathe underwater
It keeps the seal warm by reducing heat loss
It allows the seal to run faster on land
It makes the seal more attractive to land predators

questions.question: Why do living organisms have to compete with each other in their habitat?
options: Because resources are limited and they all need them to survive
Because they enjoy fighting with other species
Because there is an unlimited supply of food
Because habitats are always expanding

questions.question: Which of the following is a resource that plants frequently compete for in a crowded woodland?
options: Food
Light
Mates
Prey

questions.question: Over many generations, natural selection can cause which of the following to happen to a species?
options: The common characteristics of the species can change and evolve
Individual organisms will change their genes during their lifetime
The species will immediately stop reproducing
The species will turn into mineralised fossils within one generation

questions.question: In science, what is a "scientific theory"?
options: A random guess that has no evidence to support it
A general explanation, developed from evidence, that explains many different examples
A rule that is only true in a laboratory
An idea that cannot be tested by any scientist

questions.question: Which statement best describes how new advantageous features appear in a population?
options: They are planned in advance by the organisms
They appear randomly and are maintained by natural selection
They are chosen by the environment to suit a specific purpose
They are created by individuals practicing new skills

questions.question: If a dog loses a leg in an accident, its offspring are still born with four legs. Why is this?
options: Changes in the features of an individual within its lifetime are not evolution
The dog will learn to regrow its leg
Only dominant physical injuries are passed on to offspring
The environment always repairs genetic damage

questions.question: What is a fossil?
options: The preserved skin of an animal that died recently
The mineralised remains or traces of once-living organisms
A model of an animal made by modern scientists
An organ that has dried out in the sun

questions.question: What do fossils of dinosaurs, which are no longer found alive today, show us about these species?
options: They are currently hibernating underground
They have gone extinct
They evolved into single-celled organisms
They did not need resources to survive

questions.question: Which of the following is true about using fossil evidence to understand the history of life?
options: Fossils give us a complete and perfect record of every organism that ever lived
There are limitations to the conclusions and explanations we can make from fossil evidence
Fossils can tell us exactly what sound an animal made
Fossil evidence is always incorrect and cannot be trusted

questions.question: Why can a person who builds large muscles by lifting weights not pass these large muscles directly to their children?
options: Large muscles are a genetic trait that is too heavy to inherit
Environmental variation is not heritable and cannot be passed on to offspring
Muscles are only inherited from the mother, not the father
Lifestyle changes only affect the offspring after they reach adulthood

questions.question: Which type of variation is heritable and can be passed on to offspring?
options: Variation caused by genetic information
Variation caused by physical injuries
Variation caused by dye used on hair
Variation caused by losing a limb in an accident

questions.question: According to the theory of natural selection, which individuals in a population are most likely to survive to reproduce?
options: The largest individuals only
The fittest and best adapted individuals
The individuals that do not compete for resources
The oldest individuals in the population

questions.question: How does natural selection cause advantageous features to become more common in each generation of offspring?
options: Organisms decide to pass on only their best features
Fitter individuals are more likely to survive, reproduce, and pass on their heritable features
The environment directly changes the DNA of the parents to make them stronger
All weaker organisms voluntarily stop reproducing

questions.question: Based on scientific evidence, approximately how long ago was the Earth formed?
options: 4.5 million years ago
450 thousand years ago
4.5 billion years ago
45 billion years ago

questions.question: When does scientific evidence suggest the first living organisms (microorganisms) appeared on Earth?
options: Around 3.8 billion years ago
Around 3.8 million years ago
Around 500 million years ago
Around 200 thousand years ago

questions.question: According to scientific evidence, which of these groups of organisms appeared most recently in Earth's history?
options: First land plants
First mammals
Modern humans
Microorganisms
